steps.content: Out of breath, Christina arrives at the Sunset Club. It's a major hotel in Eastside, usually bustling with people. Today, there are even more people gathered outside—all reporters and bystanders who were forced to leave the scene.
Of course, there's also a group of Eastside sheriffs and FAC soldiers who have come late to clear the scene.

steps.speaker: Reporter A
steps.content: Gossip TV Reporting! Why is the Public Security Bureau of Eastside still sealing off the scene? What secrets are they hiding?

steps.speaker: Reporter B
steps.content: Can you tell us what the FAC's compensation case has to do with this case? Were there any Sinners involved in the case?

steps.speaker: Reporter A
steps.content: Why does this public security case involve the FAC? Is this within their jurisdiction?! Is the killer seeking revenge because the FAC pocketed the funds?!

steps.speaker: Passerby
steps.content: Me! Interview me! This is definitely related to the FAC's recent agenda! They can't hide the truth forever!

steps.speaker: Reporter B
steps.content: Some say the FAC is not a shield protecting the city, but a dangerous organization secretly undermining its security. What's your comment on this?
The clamor and intermittent flashes make the scene increasingly chaotic.

Christina remains silent, trying her best to squeeze through the crowd. The shouting reporters are easily pushed aside by her, and the detectives guarding the scene let her through after glancing at her intern ID.
Inspector Dole stands at the hotel entrance, shaking his head when he sees her.

steps.speaker: Dole
steps.content: No need to look. The scene is no longer useful.

steps.speaker: Christina
steps.content: What do you mean by "no longer useful"?

Despite his words, she insists on going in. First, she's stunned by the astonishing scene, then immediately understands what the inspector meant—Even though the scene is now sealed off, the first people to enter were reporters who got wind of the news. Their curiosity is enough to destroy everything.
